Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original score used DataReportal's 86.2% 'mobile connections' figure, which is SIM/connections-based and can include multiple SIMs per person — not the 'unique mobile subscriber penetration' the variable actually requires. GSMA Intelligence's own Rwanda-specific report (Assessing Rwanda's Mobile Tax, Dec 2024) gives unique mobile subscriber penetration as 39% in 2023 (up from 34% five years earlier, forecast 47% by 2028). 39% falls in the '25-39%' band; corrected from 5 to 2.

revision_notes: GSMA Intelligence's Rwanda-specific analysis (Dec 2024) puts smartphone penetration at 22% in 2023, below the East African (32%) and Sub-Saharan African (49%) averages; a Rwanda Revenue Authority official was separately quoted (Aug 2025) stating smartphone penetration is 'less than 25%'. Both are far below the 60-79% originally coded, which relied on a general Africa-wide GSMA report rather than Rwanda-specific data. Corrected from 4 to 2.
